translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He who, in the past, was perceived as 'I am that' by the intellect, deluded and obscured by tamas, upon the complete destruction of that (false identification), the realization of Brahman-as-Atman becomes unobstructed.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The treasure of Brahmananda is encircled and protected within the Self by the terrible serpent of ego, endowed with great power, and guarded by the three heads of the fierce goddess of Gunamaya. The wise one, wielding the great sword of Vijnana (discriminative knowledge) from the Shruti, severs the three heads, uproots this serpent, and is fit to enjoy this blissful treasure.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As long as there is even the slightest manifestation of disease or defect in the body, how can the ego, which is similarly afflicted, be fit for liberation for the yogi?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the complete cessation of the 'I'-sense and the dissolution of all its manufactured conceptual diversities, by the direct discrimination of the true Self, one realizes 'I am That' (the Absolute).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Immediately abandon the notion 'I am the doer' in the ego; dwell in your true state, which is the reflection of the Self in the modifications of the mind. This samsara—filled with birth, death, old age, and sorrow—is nothing but the result of superimposition upon your true nature, the blissful form of pure Consciousness.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For the One, unchanging, all-pervading Consciousness, whose nature is Bliss and whose fame is immaculate, there is no transmigration whatsoever without the superimposition of 'I' (on the Self).

translations.text: Therefore, having renounced the mental modifications originating from the 'I'-notion, and having abandoned attachment due to the attainment of the Supreme Truth, one remains silent, absorbed in the bliss of the Self, as the complete Self, in Brahman, without any conceptual distinctions.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Even if the great 'I' (ego) is uprooted, it may again be re-drawn, if the mind lingers for even a moment; like a cloud in the rainy season, reviving hundreds of distractions, it reactivates the mind's projections.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The space of the ego, the enemy, must be entirely restrained and never granted to the contemplation of sense objects; it is this very restraint that becomes the life-giving water for the withered jambīra tree (the body).

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How can one who is established as the body-mind complex be the distinct desire-fulfilling agent? Therefore, attachment to objects alone, due to the perception of duality, is the cause of bondage in samsara.

translations.text: Nourished by those two (ignorance and desire), it gives birth to the cycle of samsara for the Self. Through the firmness of the vasana of existence as Brahman, the triad dissolves everywhere and always.

translations.text: Just as a seaweed, once pulled out, does not remain even for a moment, so too does Maya cover the wise man even when he turns away from external objects.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: If the mind, even slightly, turns away from its goal (Brahman), it falls down step by step, just as a ball dislodged from play rolls down a flight of stairs.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The mind enters into sense objects and imagines their qualities; from correct imagination arises desire, and from desire arises action in the individual.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore, for the discriminative knower of Brahman in samadhi, there is no death greater than negligence. He who is fully concentrated attains perfection; be fully concentrated, be vigilant.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Thereupon, the loss of one's true nature causes one to fall downward; for one who has fallen, without destruction, no ascent is seen.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore, abandon all volitional thoughts, for they are the cause of all miseries. He who, while alive, attains liberation, and in the disembodied state is truly free—whosoever perceives even a trace of duality, the Yajurveda declares, is afraid.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whenever the discerning intellect, even in the infinite Brahman, perceives even a minute difference, then fear arises for that very one who sees it as distinct due to negligence.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whoever, in this perceived world — which is forbidden by hundreds of scriptural and logical authorities — identifies himself as the doer, attains a new layer of suffering upon suffering, just as one who performs a forbidden act becomes impure.

translations.author: Hindi Translation

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: One who is devoted to the pursuit of Truth attains eternal, supreme identity as the Self; but one who is attached to the pursuit of the false perishes. This is evident, just as the thief and the non-thief are clearly distinguished.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sannyasin, abandoning the attachment to the unreal, which is the cause of bondage, should abide solely in the self-awareness of 'I am Brahman'. Indeed, this steadfastness in Brahman, through direct experience, removes the sorrow caused by supreme ignorance.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: संन्यासी, जो बंधन का कारण है असत् के साथ आसक्ति को त्यागकर, केवल 'मैं ब्रह्म हूँ' इस आत्मदृष्टि से स्थित होना चाहिए। निश्चय ही, ब्रह्म में स्वानुभूति द्वारा इस निष्ठा से परम अविद्या के कार्य का दुःख नष्ट हो जाता है।

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: External attachment increases the fruit of bad tendencies, making them ever greater; knowing this through discrimination, one should abandon external pursuit and constantly engage in the inquiry of the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: When the mind is restrained from external objects, its clarity arises; in that clarity of mind, the Supreme Self is seen. When that is clearly perceived, the bondage of birth and death is destroyed; external restraint is the path to liberation.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: जब मन को बाह्य विषयों से निरोधित किया जाता है, तो उसकी प्रसन्नता उत्पन्न होती है; उस मन की प्रसादता में परमात्मा का दर्शन होता है। जब यह स्पष्ट रूप से दृष्ट होता है, तो जन्म-मरण का बंधन नष्ट हो जाता है; बाह्य निरोध ही मुक्ति का मार्ग है।

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Who is the true scholar? One who discriminates between the real and the unreal, whose authority is the Shruti, and who sees the Supreme Truth. Knowing this, the aspirant should not cling to the unreal, just as a child clings to a shadow for fear of falling.

translations.author: Hindi Translation
translations.text: कौन सच्चा पंडित है? वह जो सत्य और असत्य के बीच विवेक करता है, जिसका प्रमाण श्रुति है, और जो परमार्थ को देखता है। इसे जानकर, मुमुक्षु असत्य का आश्रय नहीं लेगा, जैसे एक बच्चा गिरने के डर से छाया को पकड़े रहता है।

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Attachment to the body and other adjuncts is not liberation; the liberated one has no identification with the body and the like. Just as deep sleep does not have waking, and waking does not have dream, so too they differ in their qualities and substrata.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Having known the Self as the support in all moving and non-moving things, both within and without, and having renounced all adjuncts, one who abides as the indivisible, complete Self — that one is liberated.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: By the all-pervading Self, the cause of bondage and liberation is none other than the identification with the All-Self; there is nothing higher than this. This identification with the All-Self arises in one who has the firm conviction of the Self, when the objects of perception are grasped.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: How can the non-apprehension of the seen (the world) be possible for one who identifies with the body and whose mind is entangled in the experience of external objects, engaged in various actions? It must be diligently practiced by those who have renounced all duties and actions, who are established in the eternal Self, and who are seekers of the ever-blissful Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The ego, which has risen with the power of identification, cannot be destroyed even by the most learned scholars in a moment. But those vasanas that are rendered motionless by the unbroken state of nirvikalpa samadhi — they indeed become extinct, boundless and endless.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The victory over the projecting power (vikṣepa) is difficult to achieve when the veiling power (āvaraṇa) remains unremoved. But when the distinction between the Seer and the seen is as clear as water and milk, the veiling power dissolves by itself in the Self, and without any doubt, the projecting power also ceases—because it is unreal.

translations.text: Right discrimination, born of clear insight, by separating the Seer and the seen—their essential nature—cuts asunder the bond of delusion created by Maya; from whom one is liberated, there is no more rebirth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Just as iron, when united with fire, appears to glow as if it were fire itself, so does the intellect, through association with the real (Brahman), manifest itself in the form of the sense-objects and their substrata. This dual phenomenon (subject and object) is unreal, as it is perceived only in delusion, dreams, and mental fantasies. Hence, all modifications of Prakriti, oriented toward the ego, ending in the body and sense-objects, are all transient. In a moment, they appear otherwise; yet the Self alone is never anything but non-existent (asat) — it is never otherwise.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Supreme Self is eternal, non-dual, indivisible, pure consciousness, the witness of the intellect and other adjuncts, distinct from the real and the unreal, the object indicated by the sense of 'I', and a mass of immediate, ever-existent bliss.
